key_concepts: A mixture is a physical combination of two or more materials without chemical changes.
Homogeneous mixtures have uniform appearance and evenly distributed components.
Heterogeneous mixtures have non-uniform appearance and recognizable phases.
Colloids have tiny particles evenly scattered in a dispersed medium and do not settle.
Suspensions have particles that do not completely dissolve in a liquid.
Solutions consist of a solute that dissolves and a solvent that does the dissolving.
Water, vinegar, and alcohol are common solvents.
Heating, stirring, and crushing make a solute dissolve faster.
Temperature, particle size, amount of solvent, and nature of solute affect solubility.
Filtration separates solid particles from a liquid using a filter.
Evaporation recovers dissolved solids such as salt from seawater.
Decantation, magnetic separation, and sieving separate different kinds of mixtures.
